verdict: The materials are now right — ledger rows, Didone figures, italic punch words are the onboarding's own language, so nothing here reads AI-generated; it reads like a careful team's second draft. But the pages are stacked, not composed: every screen pours its content into the top 45% at near-uniform optical weight and lets the bottom third die above the tab bar, where the benchmark gives each page one owner and sets its emptiness AROUND the thought (beat 19 floats the headline at optical center; beat 10 dares a whole empty page under one sentence). Home-day is a 300-euro screen with the right instincts; evening and the becoming cover are 90-euro screens wearing the right clothes; nothing yet is the 900-euro signature object. Designed materials, engineered gravity.

compositions.composition: A broadsheet with three gravities instead of one stack. Top: date eyebrow 12pt letterspaced, then the kept line at 56-60pt over two lines ("snap the / next plate", next in italic), sitting ON a full-bleed hairline rule that runs to the right edge and terminates in the ✦ seal (seal on the rule, not floating beside the text), one 17pt sub beneath. Center-left: the day's figure — 860 at ~100pt with italic "calories" run-in, one 15pt line below it. Foot: the two-row ledger (overnight fast / counts tomorrow; steps / 6,420) bottom-anchored to sit just above the tab bar. The emptiness then lives in the MIDDLE of the page, between numeral and ledger — composed air, like beat 19's floating center — instead of dying at the bottom.

One thought: the day closing. "closing the day." alone at ~56pt as the only headline on the page. Beneath it, one continuous ledger column, five rows on hairlines: protein / 62 of 90g; tomorrow / a balanced day; felt / proud · okay · tender (bare serif words as the tappable value — the chosen one turns deep rose italic, no pill outlines); still open / snap a meal ↗; and the last row IS the journal — the italic prompt "best plate today?" as label with a bare hairline writing-line as value. Zero outlined shapes, zero second headlines; the whole page is one typeset closing entry, bottom half left as evening air.

A true cover, one masthead. Top: a single eyebrow line, BECOMING · WEEK 2 OF 20 · FINDING STEADY, 12pt letterspaced. The headline drops to optical center (first ink ~a third down the page, beat-19 gravity): "this week: protein / earlier in the day." at 52-56pt, one 17pt dek beneath, the cycle note as one 20pt italic deep-rose line with its heart. Lower third earns the cover's single image: her latest plate photo tipped in as a 120pt-wide 3:4 rectangle rotated ~2 degrees, editorial still-life, the only photograph on the page. "talk it through ↗" bottom-anchored above the fore-edge ticks, and the ticks get real ink — 3pt marks at ~30% cocoa so the book's fore-edge is actually visible instead of rumored.

(Captures 04/05 arrived byte-identical to the cover, so proposed sight-unseen.) Law for every spread: one figure, one number, one sentence. Weight: the trend line drawn full-bleed edge to edge with no axes, no frame, no card; her current weight hung on the line's end as a ~96pt Didone numeral with unit run-in; one 20pt serif caption at the foot. Pacing: the mounds figure alone at 60% page height, its single insight sentence at the foot, every numeric label stripped except one. Whatever cannot justify 96pt or a full bleed does not board the spread.

The typeset two-voice page — already nearest the bar. Masthead: jeni at ~40pt italic with ONE clean eyebrow line (kill the overprint). The conversation stays bubble-less but becomes typographically two-voiced: coach in roman cocoa DMSans ~20pt ragged-left; her lines move to italic serif ~20pt deep rose ragged-right, so the exchange reads as printed correspondence rather than aligned chat. Day breaks as centered 11pt letterspaced caps with short hairlines either side. Input: a bare baseline hairline the full text width, italic serif placeholder, bare send glyph — the page's last printed rule, not a form.

checklist_iconic.diagnosis: The kept line has the right instrument — serif vow, hairline, hollow ✦ — but it is set at ~44pt in the top-left corner like an article title, its seal drifts unattached beyond the rule, and it shares the page at equal optical weight with a 76pt numeral and a two-row ledger. Nothing on it shows state, history, or ceremony: there is no visible difference between a promise and a kept promise, so a screenshot of it says nothing. Signatures are composed, singular, and slightly strange; this is tasteful and interchangeable.
checklist_iconic.proposal: THE SIGNED RULE. The day's one line at 56-60pt over two lines, seated on a full-width 0.5pt baseline rule that runs to the right edge where the hollow ✦ seal sits ON the rule like wax on a fold. When she does the thing: the rule inks left-to-right (0.5pt to 1.5pt cocoa sweep), the line itself is struck through slowly in deep rose — the onboarding's strike-the-fear gesture inverted into strike-the-kept — and the seal fills and turns 45 degrees. The page is signed, not checked. Prior days accumulate at the foot as a ledger of small struck lines (day 11 · day 10 · day 9), so the screenshot everyone posts is a cream page of crossed-out vows with today's vow still open above them. Buildable with the locked materials: one strikethrough width animation, one hairline weight animation, one filled/hollow ✦ swap, deep rose #7A2E3F ink.

becoming_pageturn: Paper first, ink second. Paged horizontal ScrollView with .scrollTargetBehavior(.paging); each page's type block wears a .scrollTransition that lags the paper: outgoing content tracks at ~0.85x of scroll offset (a 15% parallax drag, the weight of a lifted page) while a 10-12% cocoa gradient shade rises on the trailing edge — the shadow under a turning leaf, no new colors needed. The incoming headline enters 8pt low and 96% scale and settles ~120ms AFTER the page snaps, with one soft haptic tick at the snap — that deliberate lag between page-land and type-settle is the printed-page feel; simultaneous arrival is what makes carousels feel like app tabs. The fore-edge ticks at the foot ink-fill one tick per spread with a small spring, so position is read on the book's edge, not on dots. Visuals re-arm per swipe as they already do — each spread prints itself freshly.
one_move: Build the signed rule and give it the page: the kept line at 56-60pt on a full-bleed hairline with the ✦ seal seated on the rule, the strike-the-kept inking gesture on completion, and yesterday's struck vows collecting at the foot — with the ledger bottom-anchored so Home's emptiness moves to the middle of the page. It is one screen and one interaction, it converts the app's most-seen surface from an article into a signature object built entirely from the locked materials, and its grammar (rule, seal, strike) is already the founder-signed grammar of the onboarding — the rest of the app then has a gravity to imitate.
